title: Recording a Concern Under the Workmanship Warranties: Conditions and Time Limits
content:
**Rule.** Under the Workmanship Warranties, a concern is recorded against the coverage whose source work it concerns. The coverage is in active status. The customer on file still owns the vehicle: the vehicle's owned-through date is empty. The concern is reported no later than the plan's concern report window days after the customer discovered it. Days are calendar days counted from the discovery date the customer states, as day zero, and a report on the last day is in time. For a plan with a term, the concern is reported no later than term months calendar months after the issued date. Months are calendar months from the issued date; when the issued day does not exist in the end month, the term ends on that month's last day, and a report on the end date is in time. The odometer is recorded at report where the plan requires the odometer reading at report.

## The four conditions

| Condition | Evidence | Whose word governs |
|---|---|---|
| The coverage is in active status | The status of that coverage | Company record |
| The customer on file still owns the vehicle: the vehicle's owned-through date is empty | The owned-through date on that vehicle's record | Company record |
| The concern is reported no later than the plan's concern report window days after the customer discovered it | The discovery date of the concern on that coverage | The customer's statement of when they first noticed it |
| For a plan with a term, the concern is reported no later than term months calendar months after the issued date | The issued date of that coverage | Company record |

Each condition is read against the coverage the concern is recorded on and that coverage's vehicle, before the concern is recorded.

## Counting the report window

- The clock starts on the discovery date the customer states, which is day zero.
- The days are calendar days.
- The report is in time when it falls no later than the last day of the window; a report on the last day is in time.

Boundary cases (hypothetical dates, a 10-day window): discovery stated as 1 June. Day zero is 1 June, the last day of the window is 11 June. A report on 11 June is in time; a report on 12 June is later than the window.

The same discovery date under a 30-day window gives a last day of 1 July: a report on 1 July is in time, a report on 2 July is later than the window.

## Counting the term limit

- The limit applies only to a plan with a term; a lifetime-while-owned plan has no term limit on reporting.
- The clock starts on the issued date recorded on the coverage, and runs the plan's term months in calendar months.
- When the issued day does not exist in the end month, the term ends on that month's last day.
- A report on the end date is in time.

Boundary cases (hypothetical dates, a 12-month term): issued 15 March 2025, end date 15 March 2026; a report on 15 March 2026 is in time, a report on 16 March 2026 is later than the term. Issued 29 February 2024, end date 28 February 2025; a report on 28 February 2025 is in time, a report on 1 March 2025 is later than the term.

## Odometer at report

Where the plan requires the odometer reading when the concern is reported, the odometer is recorded at report.
